tagline: Up the Clearwater to the pass Lewis and Clark crossed twice.
intro: Out of Lewiston, where the Clearwater meets the Snake, US 12 takes up the Clearwater and stays with it, crossing and recrossing the river through the Nez Perce Reservation, past Orofino and Kamiah. At Lowell the Selway and the Lochsa join to make the Middle Fork, and the road follows the Lochsa up into the Bitterroot Mountains.

The top is Lolo Pass, 5,233 feet, on the Montana line. Lewis and Clark came over it westbound through the snow in September 1805 and back again the next June. The highway took until 1962. A branch, Idaho 13, leaves the river at Kooskia for the Camas Prairie and Grangeville.

moments.title: Orofino
moments.text: Five miles downstream at Canoe Camp, the expedition built five dugout canoes and set off for the Pacific on October 7, 1805.

moments.title: Heart of the Monster
moments.text: A mound near Kamiah marks where Coyote threw down the heart of a monster that had been eating all the animals, and from the scattered remains sprang the Nez Perce peoples.

moments.title: Lolo Pass
moments.text: At the pass in August 1962 the governors of Idaho and Montana dedicated the road by cutting through a cedar log with a two-man crosscut saw.

practical: Winding two-lane road with passing lanes and slow-vehicle turnouts. Winter can bring black ice in the canyons and snow higher up. Above Lowell the next services, limited, are at Powell, 13 miles west of the pass.
